sources.entry: sqlite-graph-memory - MCP server and CLI that gives coding agents recall over a folder of markdown notes, following [[wikilinks]] as a graph in one SQLite file. #opensource #free #mcp

summary.one_liner: An MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code) recall from a folder of markdown notes by combining vector search with a graph built from [[wikilinks]] stored in one SQLite file.
summary.what_it_does: It builds an index over any folder of markdown files (Obsidian vaults included) using sgm-index, embedding notes with a multilingual E5 model and storing vectors and wikilink structure in a single SQLite file. The sgm-mcp server and sgm-ask CLI then answer queries by first retrieving entry points via vector search, expanding one hop along [[wikilinks]], and reranking with a cross-encoder. Re-indexing only re-embeds new or changed notes, tracked by a manifest, unless --full is passed. The README also describes an optional PageRank lane (off by default, enabled with SGM_PPR=1 or --ppr) and an evaluation harness (eval/run_eval.py, eval/run_ablation.py) that scores vector-only versus vector+graph retrieval per query class. The search layer is read-only over the notes. The README states there is no telemetry.
use_cases: give Claude Code, Cursor or Codex persistent memory of my own notes
search an Obsidian vault semantically from an AI agent
find notes linked to a note via wikilinks
build a local recall index over a markdown folder
evaluate whether graph expansion improves note retrieval
run a private, offline-style note search without a graph database
how_to_run: claude mcp add sqlite-graph-memory -e BRAIN_INDEX_DIR=$HOME/.sgm-index -- uvx --python 3.12 --with 'sqlite-graph-memory[lite]' sqlite-graph-memory
sgm-ask --ab "In which programming language is the tool behind Project Ouzel written?"

Add an mcpServers entry (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Zed, Windsurf) or [mcp_servers] block (Codex) that runs uvx with --with 'sqlite-graph-memory[lite]' sqlite-graph-memory and sets BRAIN_INDEX_DIR to an absolute path
notable: Graph retrieval without graph extraction: uses existing [[wikilinks]] as the graph inside one SQLite file, with no graph database or ETL step
Built-in evaluation harness that scores title, body, bridge and temporal query classes in vector-only and vector+graph modes against a frozen gold set
Optional personalized PageRank lane over the wikilink graph, fused with the reranker by RRF, off by default
[lite] extra runs on ONNX Runtime without torch (about 155 MB installed per the README's Windows measurement)
Index built by either backend (ONNX or torch) is searchable by the other
caveats: Heavier installs use torch: the [embeddings] extra is about 879 MB on an x86_64 Mac per the README; Intel Mac and older macOS users must pin Python 3.12 or get an older release without [lite]

On Windows, the first MCP recall can take a long time (89 s in one clean-install example), and the default MCP deadline is 180 s in 0.3.5+ and a fixed 60 s on 0.3.3 and earlier; the MCP client's own tool timeout must also allow the call

The PageRank lane is off by default and the README says its published bridge numbers were not re-run from the published package; the README calls the project a working pilot with the graph benefit measured mainly on the maintainer's own vault
